description:
crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/mod.rs carries a 'Quick start' example that is `no_run`, so it compiles but has never been executed. Running it verbatim fails: methane/ethane, 10 stages at 101325 Pa / 200 K, reflux_ratio(2.0) + product_molar_flow(0.5) with PengRobinson gives ColumnError::NotConverged { iterations: 100, error: 2.15e-4 } from the default Wang-Henke solver.

A benzene/toluene case on the same shape converges fine (8 stages, Ideal package, feed on stage 4: Wang-Henke 16 iterations to 6.9e-7; Naphtali-Sandholm 1 iteration; top 355.4 K, bottom 376.2 K, x_benzene 0.846 -> 0.154), so the API in the example is right and only the numbers are bad.

Either retune the example to a converging case or say plainly that it is illustrative and will not converge. As written it is a trap: the first thing a reader copies fails, and the failure looks like a solver bug rather than a badly-posed column.

Found while checking how to run the column code from the Python bindings.
title: columns: the module-doc quick start does not converge as written

description:
AGREED WITH MAINTAINER 2026-09-14: the current wiring is not good, and the measured penalty is real rather than theoretical.

WHAT IT IS NOW

DhGeometry::Cls holds Mutex<(ClsMedium, u64)> and DhGeometry::Scls holds Mutex<(SclsMedium, u64)>. MaterialQuery::material_at takes &self and the trait requires Sync, so a stateful sampler needs interior mutability, and the only thing reached for was a lock. Every single point query in the transport loop therefore takes and releases a mutex — and delta tracking makes one query per virtual collision, which is the innermost loop in the whole code.

THREE SEPARATE DEFECTS, NOT ONE

1. Throughput. On the bare-pebble run CLS came out 0.51x (about 2x SLOWER than exact delta tracking) where the geometry-only benchmark says it should be 2.5-3x faster. The mutex is not the whole explanation — homogenisation also moves cost into cross-section evaluation, tracked separately as op-qolc — but it is a known contributor that is pure overhead.

2. It defeats the multi-threaded backend entirely. One lock shared by every thread serialises the hottest call in the program, so ComputeType::CpuMultiThread cannot scale for CLS or SCLS. That is not a tuning problem, it is the wrong shape.

3. It destroys reproducibility off the single-threaded path. The sampler consumes from one stream seeded by PebbleParams::seed; threads take the lock in arrival order, so the stream is consumed in a different order every run and the eigenvalue moves by of order its own statistical error. DhUniverse::keff documents this honestly today, but documenting a defect is not fixing it.

A FOURTH, INTRODUCED BY THE SCLS FIX

MaterialQuery::begin_history() landed 2026-09-14 so SCLS can reset its retention window per history. DhUniverse's impl does it by 'guard.0 = template.clone()', cloning a SclsMedium — which owns Vec<ParticleHistory> and Vec<FlightSegment> — once per source neutron. That is an allocation per history on top of the lock.

THE SHAPE THAT WOULD BE RIGHT

Give MaterialQuery an associated per-history state, so a stateful sampler gets exclusive &mut access with no lock at all:

    pub trait MaterialQuery: Sync {
        type History;
        fn begin_history(&self, gen: usize, index: usize) -> Self::History;
        fn material_at(&self, state: &mut Self::History, p: Position) -> Option<usize>;
    }

Stateless closures set type History = () and ignore it, so the blanket impl still covers every existing caller. The driver creates the state once per history at the same point begin_history() is called today and passes &mut through delta_flight/transport_history.

This fixes all four at once: no lock (throughput), per-thread state (scales), a stream seeded deterministically from (generation, history index) rather than from lock arrival order (reproducible on ANY backend, which is strictly better than what the single-threaded path gives today), and reuse of one allocation per history instead of a clone.

Note this is a strictly larger change than the 2026-09-14 seam change, because material_at gains a parameter and the blanket impl no longer hides it from private call sites inside keff_delta.rs. Every public entry point stays source-compatible for closure callers.

CHECK IT AGAINST

- CLS and SCLS eigenvalues must be unchanged within statistics on the single-threaded backend.
- A multi-threaded CLS run must reproduce the single-threaded one exactly, which is the property that does not hold today.
- Re-run examples/dh_keff_vv.rs and see how much of CLS's slowdown was the lock; that number is the answer to 'was this worth doing'.

Related: op-we7r (verify the SCLS reset actually restores SCLS behaviour), op-qolc (isolate cross-section vs geometry cost), op-cc7o (the ring-RPT mislabel that surfaced all of this).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Filed upstream as GitHub issue #205 (theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend), 2026-09-14, with the unit-cell measurements: delta 1.37765 +/- 0.00751 in 94.9 s, CLS 1.35540 +/- 0.00669 in 104.1 s (0.91x), SCLS 1.35998 +/- 0.00643 in 108.4 s (0.88x). Both approximations slower than the exact method they exist to accelerate.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: CORRECTION 2026-09-14 (GitHub #205 comment): all five V&V arms ran on ComputeType::CpuSingleThread (KeffSettings::default()), so the timing comparison is thread-matched and fair — but the measured 0.91x/0.88x is NOT evidence for the lock. On one thread the mutex is uncontended (one atomic CAS + one store), so the slowdown is mostly CLS/SCLS's own chord sampling plus the cross-section effect in op-qolc. Defects 2 (multithreading defeated) and 3 (reproducibility destroyed) follow from the shape of the code and are untouched; defect 1's magnitude is unmeasured. The measurement that would settle it: re-run the five arms under CpuMultiThread(Auto) — delta should scale with core count, CLS/SCLS should not, and the CLS eigenvalue should move run to run. If CLS scales fine, this bead is wrong about its own premise and should be closed.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
MEASURED 2026-09-14 via examples/dh_thread_scaling.rs (400 hist x [8+20], 4 cores). Results posted to GH #205.

  delta tracking        2.79s -> 1.01s   2.77x
  chord-length sampling 3.01s -> 1.54s   1.95x
  naive homogenisation  6.05s -> 1.90s   3.18x

PREDICTION 1 confirmed: delta scales 2.77x.
PREDICTION 2 REFUTED: CLS scales 1.95x, not the ~1.0x a serialised arm would give. The lock is held only for the point query; the cross-section evaluation that dominates each step is outside it, so contention is low. The throughput half of this bead does not survive measurement, and it is the half argued most confidently.
PREDICTION 3 CONFIRMED with a clean control: two identical-seed multi-threaded CLS runs gave 1.21189 and 1.18161 (+3028 pcm against 1721 pcm statistical), while the same pair on delta tracking -- no lock -- gave 1.20969 twice, bit-identical. The non-reproducibility belongs to the lock, not the backend.

SCOPE SHOULD NARROW. Defects 1 and 2 (throughput, cannot-scale) should be struck. Defect 4 (SclsMedium clone per history) is already gone, fixed in 8b44615e7 as a side effect of a more serious SCLS bug. Only reproducibility remains live, and it likely does NOT need the associated-per-history-state redesign proposed here -- a per-history RNG substream derived from (generation, index) would fix it without removing the lock. Suggested retitle: 'Multi-threaded CLS is not reproducible: the shared sampler consumes its RNG stream in lock-arrival order'.

SCLS excluded from the measurement: its retention window (~2.68 cm) exceeds the 1.9 cm fuel zone, so nothing is culled and its retained-set scan grows without bound. Recorded on DhTreatment::Scls and in 84bb23c71; a degenerate arm cannot inform a question about lock contention.

title: CLS/SCLS k-eff wiring: a global Mutex per point query is the wrong seam for a stateful sampler

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


Inspect how upstream DWSIM handles package assignment and stream transitions.

Determine: whether packages are global or per-unit/per-stream; how
`MaterialStream` associates with a package; how different packages coexist in
one flowsheet; whether DWSIM already has equivalent transition semantics; how
**enthalpy references** are handled; how electrolyte/non-electrolyte boundaries
are handled.

**Port good semantics; do not reproduce .NET object-ownership patterns.** This
fork should improve the architecture while preserving validated thermodynamic
algorithms.

Note the port has already diverged deliberately on exactly this point (the
dropped back-pointer), so the question is not "what does DWSIM do" but "what
did DWSIM's approach buy, and do we need any of it".


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: Audit upstream DWSIM property-package semantics

description:
The multicomponent flash in crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/thermo/ is real, tested and unused. Wiring it into tampines is a wiring job, not a solver-writing job -- but the wiring job is LARGER than first reported (see the correction below).

WHAT EXISTS (verified 2026-08-07):
- src/thermo/ = 26,518 lines across 35 .rs files, 223 #[test].
- src/thermo/flash.rs:194 pub fn rachford_rice_g   (cites DWSIM NestedLoops.vb line 344/553)
- src/thermo/flash.rs:206 pub fn rachford_rice_dg  (cites NestedLoops.vb line 554)
- src/thermo/flash.rs:424 pub fn nested_loops_flash<F>  -- real outer K-value iteration with convergence + error handling
- src/thermo/flash_vlle.rs:478 pub fn flash_pt_vlle -- real 3-phase VLLE with stability test, calls nested_loops_flash
- Tests: flash.rs 6 (:502, :533, :558, :581, :604, :639); flash_vlle.rs 4 (:624, :658, :690, :720).

ZERO callers of the flash routines from tampines -- and zero from anywhere in the workspace outside the dwsim crate itself.

CORRECTION to the original claim (do not repeat the "~17 call sites, pump/turbine/pipe already wired" figure -- it was a grep artifact; 13 of the 17 were doc comments):
crates/tampines/Cargo.toml:37 does declare the dependency, but tampines has only 4 `use` statements importing TYPES, and invokes exactly TWO dwsim functions in total:
  - valve.rs:35   self.opening_characteristic.kv_at_opening(...)
  - pipe.rs:88    PipeFlowCorrelation::default()
Every component evaluation method is an unwired stub returning TampinesError::NotYetImplemented:
  - pump.rs:35-38 (its own doc at :30-34 says "the underlying algebra already exists and works ... this wrapper's job ... is not yet wired up")
  - valve.rs:51 (mass_flow), heat_exchanger.rs:45, turbine.rs:40
  - turbine.rs does not even `use` dwsim; it only names it in doc links.

So the work is: finish the ~15 NotYetImplemented component wrappers over dwsim-libs, then add a PT/VLLE flash entry point for tampines' fluid state. Add a test that actually calls the flash through tampines -- today nothing does.
title: tampines: wire the tested dwsim flash + finish the NotYetImplemented component wrappers
